description: Curated source records for a code-centric world-model survey. Source counts are bibliographic records, not unique-method counts. Review depth refers to citation and mechanism checking, not experiment reproduction.

sections.title: WorldCoder-type · Programmatic Dynamics
sections.description: State-level executable dynamics: transition mechanisms, world-program induction, planning, and model repair, without generated appearance.

sections.title: Code-as-World-type · Whitebox Worlds + Generative Rendering
sections.description: Code keeps persistent state and rules over a whitebox/proxy world; a generative renderer supplies appearance.

sections.title: VibeWorlding-type · Agentic 3D World Construction
sections.description: Code specifies the full 3D world (geometry, materials, layout, and optionally physics) for conventional rendering or simulation; static scenes included.

papers.title: Procedural content generation for games
papers.summary: Historical reference on procedural content generation for games; bibliographic metadata reviewed.
papers.evidence_notes: Only bibliographic metadata was reviewed; this entry serves as historical context.

papers.title: Game Engine Learning from Video
papers.summary: Learns executable game-engine rules from video and evaluates future-state prediction and agent training.

papers.title: CSGNet: Neural Shape Parser for Constructive Solid Geometry
papers.summary: CSGNet parses visual shapes into executable constructive-solid-geometry programs.

papers.title: ShapeAssembly: Learning to Generate Programs for 3D Shape Structure Synthesis
papers.summary: ShapeAssembly represents 3D part structure with hierarchical parametric assembly programs.

papers.title: Human-Level Reinforcement Learning through Theory-Based Modeling, Exploration, and Planning
papers.summary: EMPA learns probabilistic game-engine programs and runs internal simulations for exploration and planning.

papers.title: Infinite Photorealistic Worlds Using Procedural Generation
papers.summary: Infinigen provides procedural rules for generating photorealistic geometry and materials at world scale.

papers.title: Combining Functional and Automata Synthesis to Discover Causal Reactive Programs
papers.summary: AutumnSynth alternates transition-function synthesis and automata synthesis to recover reactive programs with latent state.

papers.title: Leveraging Pre-trained Large Language Models to Construct and Utilize World Models for Model-based Task Planning
papers.summary: Uses LLMs to construct and correct PDDL domain models for sound model-based task planning.

papers.title: Holodeck: Language Guided Generation of 3D Embodied AI Environments
papers.summary: Holodeck builds language-guided 3D embodied environments through spatial constraints and optimization.

papers.title: Open-Universe Indoor Scene Generation using LLM Program Synthesis and Uncurated Object Databases
papers.summary: Open-Universe Indoor Scene Generation synthesizes executable layout constraints over uncurated object databases.

papers.title: WorldCoder, a Model-Based LLM Agent: Building World Models by Writing Code and Interacting with the Environment
papers.summary: WorldCoder synthesizes Python transition and reward models from interaction, coupling model consistency with optimistic planning.

papers.title: SceneCraft: An LLM Agent for Synthesizing 3D Scene as Blender Code
papers.summary: SceneCraft translates scene blueprints into Blender code and refines them with rendered visual feedback.

papers.title: Generating Code World Models with Large Language Models Guided by Monte Carlo Tree Search
papers.summary: GIF-MCTS searches executable Python world models using descriptions, offline transitions, and execution feedback.

papers.title: SceneMotifCoder: Example-driven Visual Program Learning for Generating 3D Object Arrangements
papers.summary: SceneMotifCoder learns editable object-arrangement programs from a few visual examples.

papers.title: Generating Symbolic World Models via Test-time Scaling of Large Language Models
papers.summary: Generates and corrects PDDL world models with Best-of-N search and fine-grained verbalized feedback.

papers.title: Text2World: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Symbolic World Model Generation
papers.summary: Text2World evaluates text-to-PDDL world-model generation with diverse domains and execution-based criteria.

papers.title: WorldModelBench: Judging Video Generation Models As World Models
papers.summary: WorldModelBench evaluates video world models using instruction adherence, physical plausibility, and human preferences.

papers.title: Synthesizing world models for bilevel planning
papers.summary: TheoryCoder combines synthesized low-level Python dynamics with supplied high-level PDDL abstractions for bilevel planning.
papers.evidence_notes: TheoryCoder is the method name; the high-level PDDL abstraction is supplied in this work.

papers.title: Imperative vs. Declarative Programming Paradigms for Open-Universe Scene Generation
papers.summary: Studies imperative and declarative scene-program representations and program-based error correction.
papers.evidence_notes: Closely related title, authors, and abstract to 2510.16147. Treat the relationship as unresolved when counting distinct methods.

papers.title: ViMo: A Generative Visual GUI World Model for App Agents
papers.summary: ViMo models mobile GUI futures through graphic and textual decomposition.

papers.title: PoE-World: Compositional World Modeling with Products of Programmatic Experts
papers.summary: PoE-World composes programmatic experts into a stochastic world model for prediction and planning.

papers.title: Finite Automata Extraction: Low-data World Model Learning as Programs from Gameplay Video
papers.summary: FAE extracts sprite-grid behavior programs from gameplay video through a constrained reactive DSL.

papers.title: Code World Models for General Game Playing
papers.summary: Synthesizes Python transitions, legal moves, termination, value heuristics, and hidden-state inference for board and card games.

papers.title: One Life to Learn: Inferring Symbolic World Models for Stochastic Environments from Unguided Exploration
papers.summary: OneLife learns conditionally activated probabilistic laws from unguided exploration in Crafter-OO.
papers.evidence_notes: Uses structured object-oriented Crafter-OO state. Distinct from Code World Models for General Game Playing (2510.04542).

papers.title: Procedural Scene Programs for Open-Universe Scene Generation: LLM-Free Error Correction via Program Search
papers.summary: Studies procedural scene programs and error correction through program search.
papers.evidence_notes: Closely related title, authors, and abstract to 2504.05482. Treat the relationship as unresolved when counting distinct methods.

papers.title: MobileWorldBench: Towards Semantic World Modeling For Mobile Agents
papers.summary: MobileWorldBench evaluates semantic mobile state transitions and their usefulness for GUI agents.

papers.title: Agent2World: Learning to Generate Symbolic World Models via Adaptive Multi-Agent Feedback
papers.summary: Agent2World uses research, development, and adaptive testing agents to generate symbolic world models and training trajectories.

papers.title: Web World Models
papers.summary: Web World Models uses typed web state and code-defined rules as the substrate for persistent, generative worlds.

papers.title: Learning Abstractions for Hierarchical Planning in Program-Synthesis Agents
papers.summary: TheoryCoder-2 learns and reuses planning abstractions in program-synthesis agents.
papers.evidence_notes: TheoryCoder-2 is the method name. The arXiv first-public date is 2026-01-31 despite the identifier prefix.

papers.title: Generative Visual Code Mobile World Models
papers.summary: gWorld predicts mobile GUI observations as renderable web code with a single vision-language model.
papers.evidence_notes: Renderable code represents a predicted observation; browser execution renders that observation.

papers.title: Code2World: A GUI World Model via Renderable Code Generation
papers.summary: Code2World learns next-GUI code generation with AndroidCode, visual revision, and render-aware learning.
papers.evidence_notes: Code2World is the GUI paper; Code2Worlds (2602.11757) is the 4D-generation paper.

papers.title: Code2Worlds: Empowering Coding LLMs for 4D World Generation
papers.summary: Code2Worlds generates object and scene programs for 4D simulation, using Blender dynamics and visual motion feedback.
papers.evidence_notes: ICML 2026 is stated on author sources; this catalogue uses the arXiv citation without an independently verified proceedings assignment.

papers.title: WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training
papers.summary: WebWorld learns a large-scale web simulator for agent training.

papers.title: Computer-Using World Model
papers.summary: Computer-Using World Model predicts textual changes and then screenshots for desktop software interactions.

papers.title: Executable World Models for ARC-AGI-3 in the Era of Coding Agents
papers.summary: Builds executable ARC-AGI-3 models with history replay, simplification, and planning.

papers.title: How Mobile World Model Guides GUI Agents?
papers.summary: Compares text, image, and renderable-code mobile predictions across reconstruction, online use, and agent-consumption strategies.

papers.title: ChronoAgentic: A Code-based Multi-Agent World Simulator for Physically Grounded Simulation Construction
papers.summary: ChronoAgentic constructs PyChrono simulation programs using planning, coding, visual review, and trajectory checks.

papers.title: Baba in Wonderland: Online Self-Supervised Dynamics Discovery for Executable World Models
papers.summary: Alice learns executable dynamics under misaligned lexical priors, using preservation conflicts to revise hypotheses and guide exploration.

papers.title: SceneCode: Executable World Programs for Editable Indoor Scenes with Articulated Objects
papers.summary: SceneCode builds editable indoor world programs with articulated objects, simulation exports, and persistent scene organization.

papers.title: OpenComputer: Verifiable Software Worlds for Computer-Use Agents
papers.summary: OpenComputer provides real software environments with structured state verification and auditable task rewards.
papers.evidence_notes: A real-software environment and verification resource, rather than a learned world-model method.

papers.title: PatchWorld: Gradient-Free Optimization of Executable World Models for Agent Environments
papers.summary: PatchWorld optimizes executable belief-state models through counterexample-guided patches and uses them for action lookahead.
papers.evidence_notes: The program maintains inferred belief state; execution consistency and target-world fidelity are separate properties.

papers.title: WorldCoder-Bench: Benchmarking Physically Grounded 3D World Synthesis
papers.summary: WorldCoder-Bench tests physically grounded 3D world synthesis using hidden runtime behavior contracts.
papers.evidence_notes: This is a 2026 world-synthesis benchmark, distinct from the evaluation of WorldCoder (2402.12275).

papers.title: Mind-Studio: Executable World Models with Lookahead Evaluation for Partially Observable Games
papers.summary: Mind-Studio constructs executable models for partially observable games and evaluates same-state multi-step lookahead fidelity.

papers.title: ScratchWorld: Evaluating If World Models Compute Executable Consequences
papers.summary: ScratchWorld uses replay-verified Scratch transitions and changed-field metrics to evaluate executable consequences.

papers.title: OPINE-World: Programmatic World Modeling with Ontology-error-Prioritized Interactive Exploration for ARC-AGI-3
papers.summary: OPINE-World jointly revises symbolic ontology, transition hypotheses, and goals through error-prioritized exploration.

papers.title: World-Time Compute with Verified Code World Models
papers.summary: World-Time Compute uses verified symbolic code worlds to generate exactly labeled trajectories for model training.
papers.evidence_notes: The first-public date is taken from source metadata (2026-07-07), rather than inferred from the arXiv identifier.

papers.title: Do Coding Agents Need Executable World Models, Simplification, and Verification to Solve ARC-AGI-3?
papers.summary: Tests executable-model discipline, simplification, and replay verification in coding agents for ARC-AGI-3.
papers.evidence_notes: All compared variants have shell/Python tools. Verification also changes interface and simplification, forming a bundled treatment.

papers.title: Program Synthesis for Simulation-Based Inference: Joint Model Selection and Parameter Estimation
papers.summary: Combines LLM-generated simulator families with neural simulation-based inference to select mechanisms and estimate parameters.

papers.title: VisualPatchWorld: Code World Models as Latent Structured Representations for Planning
papers.summary: VisualPatchWorld fits dynamics from structured state-action traces and uses visual scene graphs for replanning.
papers.evidence_notes: Dynamics induction uses structured traces. Visual planning and oracle-state induction conditions should be compared separately.

papers.title: Tycho: Active Abstraction with Programmatic World Models for ARC-AGI-3
papers.summary: Tycho actively revises abstractions and programmatic hypotheses while solving ARC-AGI-3 games.
papers.evidence_notes: Improved transition matching and the best action-efficiency result occur under different settings in the reported public-game evaluation.

papers.title: WorldClaw: Agentic 3D Open-World Generation at Scale
papers.summary: WorldClaw builds large editable 3D scenes through region planning, terrain generation, and render-guided refinement.
papers.evidence_notes: Scene generation and editable geometry are the reviewed capabilities.

papers.title: AppDeltaWorld: Transition-Grounded Delta Code World Model for Mobile GUI Agents
papers.summary: AppDeltaWorld predicts transition-grounded HTML updates with retrieved structure, visual assets, and closed-loop refinement.

papers.title: Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin
papers.summary: Twin builds a test-time digital twin and checks historical transitions before choosing actions in unknown games.

papers.title: Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain
papers.summary: Code World Model separates a coding world brain from a visual world engine through executable proxy representations.
papers.evidence_notes: The reported renderer training is a small-scale gameplay study; the real-video pipeline and trained-renderer evidence have different scopes.

papers.title: Magpie: Real-Time World Renderer for Interactive Games
papers.summary: Magpie combines persistent game-engine state and rules with a whitebox-conditioned interactive neural renderer.
papers.evidence_notes: Frame throughput and action-response latency measure different aspects of interactivity.

papers.title: Code as Worlds: Agentic Discovery of Executable World Representations for Physical Reasoning
papers.summary: Code as Worlds discovers executable physical representations through propose, instantiate, execute, render, and verify loops.

papers.title: FuncRoom-Agent: Sequential Feed-Forward 3D Functional Indoor Scene Generation
papers.summary: FuncRoom-Agent generates functional indoor scenes with a recursive DSL, sequential expert, and execution-grounded process reward.

papers.title: GUI-CC: Benchmarking Contextual Consistency of GUI World Models as Agent Environments
papers.summary: GUI-CC evaluates multi-step contextual consistency through offline reference actions and online agent loops.

papers.title: WebWorld: The Browser as a World Model for Self-Improving Web Code
papers.summary: Uses the browser to execute and verify self-improving web code against interaction contracts and preserved behaviors.

papers.title: Programmable World Model
papers.summary: Programmable World Model compiles persistent engine state, including nonvisual facts, into controls for video generation.
papers.evidence_notes: CombatStateBench is included in this paper. Its death metric checks a dead character appears, at coarse scene level.

papers.title: Recursive Code World Models: Building Complex Worlds through Recursive Scene Programs
papers.summary: Recursive Code World Models reconstruct complex scenes using recursive programs, global-local refinement, and shared reference views.
papers.evidence_notes: The reported reconstruction is static; dynamic behavior belongs to a separate evaluation axis.

papers.title: GameLogicBench: Evaluating Coding Agents on Runtime Game Logic with Tick-Level State Assertions
papers.summary: GameLogicBench checks Godot game rules at every simulation tick across varied reproducible scenarios.

papers.title: GameDirector: Decoupling Gameplay Logic from Rendering for Player-Configurable Game World Models
papers.summary: GameDirector uses visual situation estimates and explicit gameplay rules to control game-video generation.

papers.title: Code Plans, Diffusion Renders: Open-Ended Generative World Modeling
papers.summary: CoDeR coordinates executable whitebox world construction with a generative Artist for open-ended visual worlds.

papers.title: The GUI Is Not the State: Diagnosing State Aliasing in GUI World Models
papers.summary: StateAliasBench pairs identical visible GUI conditions with different futures to diagnose hidden transition state.

papers.title: EMPIRIC: Experiment-Driven Learning of Residual World Models for Robot Planning
papers.summary: EMPIRIC learns residual code that extends a physics engine with missing forces, constraints, and hidden state.
papers.evidence_notes: Geometry and object features are supplied; the physical Fan-Domino experiment is one domain demonstration.

papers.title: LEGO-Anything: Coding Agents for 3D Scene Reconstruction
papers.summary: LEGO-Anything reconstructs 3D scenes as executable programs and separates artifact, geometry, and appearance evaluation.

papers.title: Kepler: Auditable World Models for ARC-AGI-3
papers.summary: Kepler studies auditable ARC-AGI-3 world models through retrospective and conditional transition checks and cost accounting.
papers.evidence_notes: The arXiv comment names a non-archival NeurIPS 2026 workshop; it should not be labeled as a main-conference paper.

papers.title: AutoGUIWorld: Image Generators as Visual World Models for GUI Agent
papers.summary: AutoGUIWorld synthesizes GUI trajectories by planning visual consequences and iteratively editing screenshots.

papers.title: PROWBench: Do Video Models Render What the Program Specifies?
papers.summary: PROWBench compares rendered video events with executable program specifications and event logs.
papers.evidence_notes: Program logs provide event references; visual adherence is read by a VLM judge that has not been human-calibrated in the paper.

papers.title: Video2World: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive World Modeling from Embodied Videos
papers.summary: Video2World evaluates video-to-interactive-world reconstruction through geometry, dynamics, and function.

papers.title: LLM-IDEA: Identifiability-Driven Experimental Agent for Autonomous Discovery of Mechanistic World Models
papers.summary: LLM-IDEA uses identifiability-aware experimental design to distinguish mechanistic explanations.

papers.title: USDCraft: Geometrically Grounded Programmatic Modeling of Articulated 3D Assets for Simulation
papers.summary: USDCraft converts source geometry into executable modeling programs that export articulated USD simulation assets.
papers.evidence_notes: Source geometry is input, executable modeling programs are generated, and articulated USD is the exported artifact.

papers.title: Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks
papers.summary: Memento 3 revises reflective rulebooks and executable models using trajectory judgments and exact replay.
papers.evidence_notes: Self-improvement updates external rulebooks and programs while the base language model remains frozen.

papers.title: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents
papers.summary: Studies GUI world models as transition verifiers and separates screen similarity from transition correctness.

papers.title: AgentGarten: Code Worlds for Evolving Agents
papers.summary: AgentGarten connects program-defined simulation backends to a shared real-time renderer and reusable agent playbooks.
papers.evidence_notes: Reported skill reuse includes inherited written playbooks; parameter learning and matched-budget training gains require separate evidence. Mechanism review uses v1; the author list was refreshed from current arXiv metadata on 2026-10-14.

papers.title: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Human and Agent Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks
papers.summary: Interactive Newton-based toolkit exposes solver, contact-model and physical-parameter choices so humans and coding agents can refine manipulation simulations against observed behavior.
papers.evidence_notes: Simulation configuration and calibration are supported; the abstract does not establish synthesis of a new transition algorithm. State evolution is delegated to Newton. Real2sim calibration is mixed observation-driven adjustment and simulator specification. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: Write Once, Plan Many: Building Reusable Visual Planning Systems from One Scene
papers.summary: Builds reusable executable renderers, dynamics, perception and planning programs from supplied domain rules and one practice scene; execution and reconstruction checks refine programs before reuse.
papers.evidence_notes: Task schema, interfaces and rules are supplied. This is rule implementation and visual grounding, not discovery of unknown dynamics from transition data. Executable renderer code additionally maps states to RGB-D, but does not make predicted observations themselves code. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: WorldOracle: Benchmarking Action-Conditioned World Models against Real-World Executions
papers.summary: Evaluates action-conditioned robot world-model rollouts against paired physical executions across state correctness, spatial alignment, local interaction fidelity and multiview coherence.
papers.evidence_notes: An evaluation benchmark and dataset, not evidence that executable code represents or learns the evaluated models' dynamics. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: From Pixels to Executable Physics: Behavior-Grounded World Models for Embodied Action Consequence Prediction
papers.summary: Combines RGB scene reconstruction and behavior-calibrated terrain contact priors with physics simulation, using simulated motion and geometry to guide a video world model.
papers.evidence_notes: Physical-parameter/terrain specification feeds an existing simulator; no abstract evidence of synthesizing transition source code. Learned video observations update reconstruction. S is simulator-input configuration, not generated executable world-rule code. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: Neurosymbolic Learning of Interpretable World Models
papers.summary: Learns visual concept grounding while a parameter-free predictor applies supplied temporal-logic transition rules; planning differentiates through symbolic imagined trajectories.
papers.evidence_notes: Complete deterministic transition knowledge is assumed; only the encoder is trained. S/E refer to executable declarative logic, not induced program code. Fully observable deterministic environments are the reported setting. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
papers.summary: Compiles screenplay shots with spatial and event-time references, retrieves registered scene and event memories, and admits generated observations into memory only after checks.
papers.evidence_notes: Explicit geometry and event memory do not by themselves establish an executable state-transition world model. The verified abstract supports retrieval, registration and admission control, not code-generated dynamics. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: Self-Building Labs
papers.summary: Agents construct laboratory digital twins, reusable robot skills and workflows from objectives, photographs and device information, refining scene models using observations and physical feedback.
papers.evidence_notes: The paper explicitly describes Python construction of geometry, joints, simulated device APIs and an Isaac Sim USD twin. This establishes world construction/configuration; broad autonomous discovery of physical laws or chemical dynamics is not established. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: LLM Agents as Suppliers of Physical System Models: Calibration and Acceptance in Modelica
papers.summary: Studies LLM coding agents that assemble and calibrate executable Modelica physical-system models from descriptions and data, with acceptance based on behavioral fit, invariants and interpretability.
papers.evidence_notes: Models are built from library components under partially specified handovers; fitting does not identify a unique true structure. The paper explicitly distinguishes data fit from physical validity and interpretable model acceptance. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: State World Models: Execute the Rules, Generate the Pixels
papers.summary: A coding agent writes a typed game definition; a runtime executes rules over semantic and spatial state before a frozen video renderer, then admits rule-compatible visual feedback.
papers.evidence_notes: World rules are specified and frozen per episode rather than induced from unknown transition data. Rule settlement and compilation are deterministic conditional on accepted inputs; neural rendering/observation remains stochastic. Procedural previews are guidance, not predicted-observation source code. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
papers.summary: Synthesizes executable computer-use worlds spanning GUI, MCP and CLI interfaces, with replayable state-building programs and execution-based task/verifier quality gates for agent training.
papers.evidence_notes: Worlds and tasks are authored from personas and day plans; this is environment synthesis rather than identification of an unknown real system's dynamics. Generated service backends implement interaction semantics; deterministic replay verifies constructed states, not real-world fidelity. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: Events, Not Pixels: Where World Models Get the Return Wrong
papers.summary: Diagnoses return errors by replacing selected imagined transitions with real ones under matched budgets; reward/terminal events matter more than visually poor frames for the tested models.
papers.evidence_notes: This is a transition-level diagnostic study, not a new executable-code world model or a general theorem. Its interventions rely on access to real transitions and reliability-screened model-collection pairs. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
papers.summary: Evaluates agent-created Blender projects against multimodal briefs using rendered views, task rubrics and visual-quality judgments.
papers.evidence_notes: The task includes reference reconstruction and specification following; it does not establish learned state-transition programs. Some agents may use direct UI manipulation rather than code. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
papers.summary: Packages executable 3D programs with assets and verification records; a generation-and-repair harness uses execution, geometry measurements and visual feedback.
papers.evidence_notes: A large ecosystem for programmable geometry, scenes and assets. Physics examples use existing solvers; neither 2M code-condition pairs nor simulation support alone proves induction of unknown dynamics. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: GlobeBench: Evaluating Text-Based World Model Capabilities for Scalable Environment Simulations
papers.summary: Tests textual action-conditioned successor predictions against execution-derived references, combining deterministic checks with semantic judging.
papers.evidence_notes: Execution supplies ground truth, but evaluated models predict textual responses rather than executable transition code. Induction here denotes inference from trajectories, not demonstrated program induction. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: Beyond Next-Screen Prediction: The Decision Value of GUI World Models
papers.summary: Controls prediction presentation and supervision when comparing GUI lookahead with a directly learned action ranker, testing the incremental decision value of predicted screens.
papers.evidence_notes: A comparator and evaluation warning for GUI world models. It neither proposes generated transition code nor implies all world models lack decision value; its negative result is bounded to tested GUI settings. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: NeoWorld-3: From Pixels to Code-Defined Physical Worlds
papers.summary: Reconstructs editable geometry programs from visual evidence through hierarchical coding agents, differentiable parameter fitting and articulation/physics checks.
papers.evidence_notes: Core under a broad program-as-world-specification definition; not evidence of learning general physical transition laws. Differentiability is limited to supported builder operations. The linked Studio repository currently describes documentation only, not an installable implementation. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
papers.summary: A coding agent turns player requests into executable game rules; an engine owns persistent state, while a causal video model renders detailed views from low-poly proxies.
papers.evidence_notes: The transition code is authored from requested gameplay, not identified from unknown observed dynamics. Neural rendering is not predicted observation code O. Reported performance is the authors claim, not an independently reproduced result. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: SceneRig: An Agentic System for Simulation-Ready 3D Scene Reconstruction from Single Images
papers.summary: Reconstructs objects and scene layout from one image, then edits scene code and uses bounded pose search plus simulation validation to retain physically stable, visually aligned configurations.
papers.evidence_notes: Code specifies the reconstructed scene; existing simulator dynamics provide validation and rollout. Current objects are single rigid bodies, without recovered articulation or deformation. Relevant to configuration induction, not transition-law induction. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: WorldStream: Streaming Interactive 3D Worlds with Hierarchical Planning and Persistent State
papers.summary: Hierarchical planning predicts typed regional and tile specifications; fixed procedural generators compile them, while persistent records retain identities, boundary contracts and edits across streaming revisits.
papers.evidence_notes: S is the generated semantic program/configuration. E occurs in the fixed executing runtime and stateful interactions, rather than in learned or generated transition-code synthesis, so E is not assigned as a generated-program role. The paper is a bounded procedural prototype with a curated generation vocabulary; geographic conditioning is not dynamics induction. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering
papers.summary: Adapts a frozen video backbone with control and acceleration LoRAs to turn aligned structural video into detailed video, including streaming generation.
papers.evidence_notes: An enabling visual renderer for code/engine-based systems. It consumes rendered structural conditions and does not itself generate world programs, state-evolution code or observation code; neural rendering alone is not O. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V
papers.summary: Benchmarks executable-program video creation from text, images and videos with objective and model-judged measures of execution, quality and alignment.
papers.evidence_notes: Programs encode requested visual and temporal construction. This creative-generation benchmark is not an action-conditioned environment prediction benchmark; animation or state-dependency complexity alone does not establish learned world dynamics or O. Date records arXiv v1; earlier external releases were not exhaustively audited.

papers.title: Oneira: From Open-Ended Generation to Open-World Interaction in Video World Models
papers.summary: A coding agent and lightweight engine maintain an extensible world-state table, compile coarse visual conditions, and incorporate newly observed objects for persistent interaction.
papers.evidence_notes: The state table stores coarse object states and interaction outcomes; detailed motion is completed by the video generator.

papers.title: Mallea: Building, Steering, and Memorizing Worlds with Coding Agent
papers.summary: A coding agent jointly builds object structures and rules, supports runtime edits preserving unaffected state, and combines executed state with object texture memory for rendering.
papers.evidence_notes: Texture memory is tied to whitebox-defined objects. State evolution, user-requested editing, and visual memory are distinct responsibilities.

papers.title: ExeWorldBench: Benchmarking Code-Based Executable 3D World Modeling
papers.summary: Evaluates individual mechanisms, compositional mechanical systems, and intent-driven executable 3D world synthesis.
papers.evidence_notes: Benchmark targets executable world construction and mechanisms; it is not itself a learned dynamics method. Author spellings follow arXiv abstract-page metadata.

papers.title: Code2Worlds-2: Physically Plausible Agent Harness for Embodied World Simulation
papers.summary: Compiles generated visual scenes into MuJoCo-compatible worlds with physical attributes and refines executable dynamics using simulator feedback.
papers.evidence_notes: Engine dynamics are inherited; scene compilation and simulator-guided refinement are the generated contribution. Public benchmark readiness checks should be separated from method-generated-world success.

papers.title: RoleWorld: Knowledge Transfer in World Modeling with Functional Role Abstractions
papers.summary: Extracts reusable role prototypes and executable transition rules, then adapts role assignments and parameter estimates in new environments while keeping transition rules fixed.
papers.evidence_notes: Target-world adaptation changes role assignments and parameter estimates, not the fixed transition rules or LLM weights.

papers.title: EdenLive: Real-Time Generative Rendering from Any Visual Reference
papers.summary: A generative renderer maps upstream reference video, a target first frame and a prompt to enhanced video. The upstream program maintains state and rules. Released tooling also includes a prompt-to-playable-game skill and workbench.
papers.evidence_notes: S/E belong to the generated or existing upstream game, not to the neural renderer. O does not apply: predicted observations are video, not code.  Current official README confirms released code and weights. October 18 release date was not established from accessible primary history; API returned rate-limit 403. Do not label October 18 as first publication.

papers.title: Mundo: Customized World Model
papers.summary: Images are reconstructed into an editable 3D proxy. A scene program specifies objects and physical parameters; scripts and usually MuJoCo evolve state. Proxy frames condition a video renderer together with context views.
papers.evidence_notes: The scene program specifies state and simulation rules; executable scripts/physics advance it. Video is the observation, so O is absent. Authors report slow rendering, small-object interaction errors and no long-horizon memory mechanism. Demos do not establish general physical fidelity or downstream robot-training gains. Author blog explicitly gives Published October 23, 2026. This establishes the dated announcement, not an audited first code or model release.

papers.title: A Declared World Model: Language Models Write the Rules of the Scene They are Shown
papers.summary: A language model writes world rules from a labelled scene graph. A deterministic engine checks proposed actions and computes next states. Experiments test whether generated rules transfer beyond the observed layout.
papers.evidence_notes: Rules are declared as a program and executed for action acceptance and state updates; generated observation code is not established. Perception is held perfect. Abstract reports layout-bound rules from a single scene; separating facts/rules or varying layouts can improve lifting. These controlled results do not establish arbitrary visual-world reconstruction. Exact v1 posting date on the publisher page; not a claim about any earlier informal manuscript.

papers.title: StreamRender-H3: Interactive Coding Worlds with Real-time Streaming Diffusion Render
papers.summary: A three.js game engine maintains maps, rules and state, advancing on player inputs. Semantic frames connect it to a streaming MiniMax-H3 renderer. The demonstrated system separates executable simulation from generated appearance.
papers.evidence_notes: S/E belong to the explicitly included game engine. The learned renderer does not itself supply executable state dynamics; output pixels are not O-code. Published renderer evaluation is racing-specific. No standalone StreamRender-H3 paper is established; page asks citation alongside the underlying Sol-Engine paper. Issue #536 opened on October 12 discusses released StreamRender code/checkpoint. It establishes availability by that day, not initial release. Current project details may include later updates.

papers.title: VibeWorlding: Can Multimodal Agents Construct 3D Open Worlds End-to-End?
papers.summary: VibeWorlding studies an end-to-end multimodal coding agent that constructs and edits open 3D worlds in a Blender sandbox through asset retrieval, procedural editing, rendered-view feedback, and physical-feasibility checks.
papers.evidence_notes: The primary task is agentic 3D world construction and editing with VWE-Bench; it should not be counted as temporal dynamics discovery unless a separate transition model is evaluated.

papers.title: Fight World Model: Customizable Combat through Visual Interaction Proxies
papers.summary: Separates executable combat state and rule resolution from video rendering with identity- and timing-aligned interaction proxies; tests rule changes and customization.
papers.evidence_notes: The abstract describes an executable engine as the source of combat state and a deterministic proxy compiler for the renderer. This is a code-as-world design, not evidence that the combat rules were induced from unknown observations. Date follows arXiv v1 metadata; no venue assignment is inferred.

papers.title: BoxWorld: Let World Engines Control and Video Generators Render

papers.evidence_notes: CineU is included because executable engine state and agent-generated operations are central to the abstract. Cinematic choreography is the application, not the inclusion criterion. Date follows arXiv v1 metadata; no venue assignment is inferred.
